speakers: The king over all the land
meta.audience: The Lamanite king, his household, and the gathered multitude
meta.location: The land of Nephi, at the king's palace
meta.unit: The sons of Mosiah among the Lamanites (Alma 17–26)
principles: Teaching a man who asks to be taught
Giving away all to know God

world_behind.title: Aaron comes as a prisoner released
world_behind.text: Verse 2 has him introduce himself by the favor already granted: we are the brethren of Ammon, whom thou hast delivered. Alma 20 negotiated that release at swordpoint, and it is Aaron's credential at the door.

world_behind.title: The king had unfinished questions
world_behind.text: Verse 3 says he was troubled in mind because of Ammon's words, and verse 5 pins the trouble to the Spirit of the Lord. He had heard enough on the road to be unable to let it go.

world_behind.title: The Amalekites had already won a concession
world_behind.text: Verse 7 has the king say he granted them sanctuaries to worship God in. He is telling Aaron that the word God is already in circulation in his kingdom, attached to a group Aaron just failed to reach.

world_behind.title: The Great Spirit carried the exodus story
world_behind.text: Verse 9 asks whether God is the Great Spirit who brought the fathers out of Jerusalem. Lamanite tradition had kept the journey and attached it to their own name for deity.

world_behind.title: The queen holds the power of execution
world_behind.text: Verses 19 and 21 have her order Aaron killed twice, first through the servants and then through a summoned crowd. The servants refuse her on grounds of fear, which tells the reader how the palace had come to see Ammon's brethren.

world_behind.title: The proclamation is a legal act
world_behind.text: Verse 27 sends a decree through the whole kingdom, and Alma 23 opens with its content. The conversion of one man becomes policy across every land the Lamanites hold.

world_behind.title: Mormon stops the story to draw a map
world_behind.text: Verses 27 through 34 give the fullest geography in the record: the narrow strip of wilderness, the two seas, Bountiful and Desolation, the small neck of land. He supplies it at the moment the whole southern kingdom opens to preaching.

words.text: Of the flesh, and in scripture the condition of a nature ruled by appetite. Aaron lays "their carnal state" (v. 13) before the king as part of the account of the fall. The record uses the word fifteen times and the King James Bible eleven, most of them in Paul, and Mosiah 27 pairs it with fallen in exactly this sense.

To earn, to deserve as wages. The word occurs twice in this record and never in the King James Bible: here, where fallen man "could not merit anything of himself" (v. 14), and in Mosiah 2, where king Benjamin asks whether he merits any thanks. Both uses deny that a debt is owed.

cites.quote: could not merit anything of himself

spans.text: could not merit anything of himself

words.text: The wound a scorpion or a bee leaves. Aaron says the sting of death is swallowed up in the hopes of glory, borrowing Paul's cry over the open grave in 1 Corinthians 15. The word appears four times in this record, twice in Abinadi's mouth, and Aaron is quoting a resurrection text to a king who has just heard about the fall.

Calmed, brought out of anger. Twice in this chapter a crowd is pacified by the king himself. The record uses the word six times, and three of those are in Mosiah 20, where a Lamanite king likewise talks a mob down from killing.

Unoccupied, and by extension unsettled. Mormon calls the wilderness Lamanites "the more idle part" (v. 28) and says they dwelt in tents. The word appears three times in this record and eleven in the King James Bible. It is a Nephite judgment on a way of living, recorded without argument.

A place emptied and ruined. Here it names the land northward, the country of the destroyed people whose bones Zarahemla's colony found. The record uses the word twenty-two times, and the last chapters of Mormon return to this same ground to end the nation there.

phrases.term: I have been somewhat troubled in mind
phrases.text: The king explains why he is sparing lives instead of taking them. What troubles him is the generosity of Ammon on the road, and the words that came with it. He asks for teaching before anyone offers it.

phrases.term: Believest thou that there is a God?
phrases.text: Aaron's opening move, the same question Ammon put to Lamoni in Alma 18. This king answers with policy: the Amalekites say so, and he has let them build. Then he adds that Aaron's word would be enough for him.

phrases.term: Is God that Great Spirit that brought our fathers out of the land of Jerusalem?
phrases.text: The king supplies the bridge himself. He has an exodus story and a name for deity, and he asks whether the two belong together. Aaron says yes and adds creation to it.

phrases.term: He could not merit anything of himself
phrases.text: The center of Aaron's teaching, given in six words. Fallen man earns nothing; the sufferings and death of Christ do the work. A king who is about to offer his entire kingdom is told first that nothing he owns is currency.

phrases.term: The sting of death should be swallowed up in the hopes of glory
phrases.text: Paul's language over the grave, delivered to a Lamanite monarch who has never seen an epistle. Aaron has moved from the fall to the resurrection in a single verse of summary, and the king's next sentence asks how to get in.

phrases.term: What shall I do that I may be born of God
phrases.text: The jailer at Philippi asked the same thing in almost the same words. The king wants the wicked spirit rooted out of his breast, and he names the price he is willing to pay before Aaron says anything about cost.

phrases.term: I will give away all my sins to know thee
phrases.text: A phrase found once in scripture, spoken in a prayer by a man who still says "if there is a God" in the same sentence. He offers the one thing he actually owns, and the offer is accepted before the doubt is resolved.

phrases.term: Standing as though they had been the cause of his fall
phrases.text: The queen walks in on a still body and three foreigners. Mormon records the appearance from her side. Her reading of the room is reasonable, and it nearly gets four men killed.

phrases.term: He put forth his hand and raised the king from the earth, and said unto him: Stand
phrases.text: Aaron ends the crisis by ending the coma. He acts to prevent a gathering he can see coming, and one word gets the king on his feet. Abish did the same for the queen of Ishmael three chapters back.

phrases.term: Divided from the land of Zarahemla by a narrow strip of wilderness
phrases.text: The border of two nations, given once and never repeated. It runs sea to sea, and every war chapter in the rest of Alma assumes it. Mormon puts the line on paper at the moment the barrier starts coming down.

phrases.term: That they might have a country whither they might flee
phrases.text: Mormon explains Nephite strategy: hem the Lamanites in on the south, and keep the north open as an escape. The last book of the record has the Nephites making that flight and finding no ground at the end of it.

verses.label: v. 1–6
verses.title: Aaron at the palace
verses.text: He asks for his life and offers service. The king grants the life, refuses the servitude, and asks for ministry instead, because Ammon's generosity has left him troubled. His two questions are about the Spirit of the Lord and about being cast off at the last day.

verses.label: v. 7–11
verses.title: The ground laid
verses.text: Believest thou there is a God. The king answers with what the Amalekites say and what he has permitted, then says Aaron's word will be enough. He asks whether God is the Great Spirit of the exodus, hears that he is and that he made everything, and asks to be told the rest.

verses.label: v. 12–14
verses.title: The scriptures read
verses.text: Aaron begins at the creation of Adam and reads: the image of God, the commandments, the transgression, the fall, the carnal state, the plan of redemption prepared from the foundation of the world. Then merit, atonement, the bands of death, and the sting swallowed up.

verses.label: v. 15–18
verses.title: The king's question and prayer
verses.text: What shall I do to be born of God, with the wicked spirit rooted out. He offers his kingdom. Aaron names repentance and calling on God in faith. The king prostrates himself, offers all his sins in exchange for knowledge of God, and falls as if dead.

verses.label: v. 19–23
verses.title: The queen, and Stand
verses.text: She orders the killing; the servants refuse out of fear; she calls a crowd instead. Aaron raises the king by the hand with one word. The household sees it, marvels, and is converted while the king ministers to them.

verses.label: v. 24–27
verses.title: The multitude, and the decree
verses.text: The summoned crowd murmurs. The king stands among them and calms them, then has Aaron and his brethren preach in the middle of it. Afterward he proclaims through all his lands, and Mormon takes the occasion to describe them.

verses.label: v. 28–35
verses.title: The map
verses.text: The idle Lamanites in tents on the west, the driven Lamanites on the east, the Nephites holding the north at the head of Sidon, Bountiful against Desolation, a day and a half's journey across the neck, and the wisdom of leaving a road out. Then Mormon returns to the brothers.

chapter.title: This king asks to be taught
chapter.text: Lamoni had to be led to the question; his father arrives with it. He has been troubled since the road, and he opens by asking for ministry from men he could have executed.

chapter.title: Aaron uses a text
chapter.text: Verses 12 and 13 have him reading the scriptures and expounding from the creation of Adam. Where Ammon worked from the hearer's vocabulary, Aaron works from a document, and the chapter shows both methods succeeding.

chapter.title: Merit is denied before the kingdom is offered
chapter.text: The king says he will forsake everything he possesses; the doctrine he has just heard says none of it buys anything. The record keeps the offer in and lets the reader see it is unnecessary.

chapter.title: The prayer is offered with the doubt intact
chapter.text: He prays if there is a God, and if thou art God, and in the same breath gives away all his sins. The record treats an honest conditional as sufficient grounds for an answer.

chapter.title: The servants have learned something the queen has not
chapter.text: They saw the cause of the fall and will not touch Aaron. Her authority is real and it stops at the edge of what her staff has witnessed.

chapter.title: A word ends the crisis
chapter.text: Aaron sees a mob forming and raises the king with one syllable. The public miracle in this chapter is performed to prevent violence, and its first result is a household converted.

chapter.title: The proclamation makes conversion national
chapter.text: One man's belief goes out as law across every land the Lamanites hold. Alma 23 shows what it produced: seven cities and thousands of converts.

chapter.title: The map arrives with the opening
chapter.text: Mormon has withheld the geography for twenty-two chapters and supplies it here, at the moment a closed country opens. Everything from Alma 43 to Mormon 6 is fought over the ground this passage names.

applications.title: Say what has been troubling you
applications.text: The king named the thing he could not shake and asked for help with it. When something you heard weeks ago is still working on you, tell someone what it was and ask them to explain it.

applications.title: Start where their story already goes
applications.text: The king had an exodus and a name for God, and Aaron built on both. Before you supply a framework, find out what the person already carries that points the right way.

applications.title: Pray with the doubt in the sentence
applications.text: The king said if there is a God and gave away his sins anyway. You do not have to resolve the question first; say the conditional out loud and make the offer inside it.

applications.title: Act to stop the crowd forming
applications.text: Aaron saw where the gathering was heading and moved before it arrived. Where you can see a conflict assembling, do the defusing thing early instead of preparing to survive it.

questions.text: What have I heard that troubled me, and have I gone back to ask about it?
Whose word would be enough for me on something I have not settled?
What am I still trying to earn that I have been told cannot be earned?
What would I say if someone asked what I want changed in me?
What sins am I willing to give away today to know God?
When have I blamed the people standing nearest to something that frightened me?
What escape route am I keeping open, and what does keeping it cost?
